title: Cokernels of module objects are computed in $\mathcal C$
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive monoidal category whose tensor product is additive in
each variable. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$ such that
$\mathcal R\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits. Let $f\colon M\to N$ be a morphism of
$\mathcal R$-module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]) whose underlying morphism has a
cokernel $\pi\colon N\to Q$ in $\mathcal C$. Then there is a unique morphism
$\gamma_Q\colon\mathcal R\otimes Q\to Q$ with
$\gamma_Q\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\pi)=\pi\circ\gamma_N$. It is an action of $\mathcal R$ on
$Q$, and $\pi\colon N\to(Q,\gamma_Q)$ is a cokernel of $f$ in
$\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text: Write $T=\mathcal R\otimes-$, and compose maps from right to left. A cokernel of $u$ means a coequalizer of $u$ and the zero morphism: its projection $q$ satisfies $qu=0$, and every $v$ with $vu=0$ has a unique factorization through $q$. Additivity gives $T(0)=0$, since $T(0)=T(0+0)=T(0)+T(0)$. The coequalizer diagram is finite, so the hypothesis that $T$ preserves finite colimits says directly that $T\pi$ is a coequalizer of $Tf$ and $T(0)=0$, hence a cokernel of $Tf$. Apply the same hypothesis to this coequalizer: $T^2\pi$ is a cokernel of $T^2f$. Only these existing coequalizers are used; no other cokernels in $\mathcal C$ are assumed.

source.place: first paragraph, preservation of the cokernel; second paragraph, tensoring twice

proof.text: Each of $\pi,T\pi,T^2\pi$ is an epimorphism by the uniqueness just recalled: if $a q=b q$ for one of these cokernel projections $q$ of $u$, the common map $v=aq=bq$ satisfies $vu=0$, and $a,b$ are both its factorization through $q$, so $a=b$. Also $\mathbf1\otimes\pi=\lambda_Q^{-1}\pi\lambda_N$ by naturality of the left unitor, hence it is an epimorphism by this same cancellation and invertibility of the unitors. Put $a=(\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R)\otimes\pi$. Naturality gives $\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,Q}a=T^2\pi\,\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,N}$, so $a$ is an epimorphism too. This uses no assertion that $T$ preserves arbitrary epimorphisms.

source.place: second paragraph, the three cancellation maps

proof.text: The morphism axiom of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] for $f$ and the cokernel equation give $\pi\gamma_N Tf=\pi f\gamma_M=0$. The universal property of $T\pi$ from step 1 therefore supplies a unique map $\gamma_Q:TQ\to Q$ with $\gamma_Q T\pi=\pi\gamma_N$. This proves uniqueness among all maps satisfying the displayed equation, before any module axioms are imposed.

source.place: first paragraph, construction and uniqueness of the action map

proof.text:
For the unit axiom, naturality of tensoring with $\eta$ and the defining equation in step 3 give
$$\gamma_Q(\eta\otimes Q)(\mathbf1\otimes\pi)=\gamma_Q T\pi(\eta\otimes N)=\pi\gamma_N(\eta\otimes N)=\pi\lambda_N=\lambda_Q(\mathbf1\otimes\pi).$$
The third equality is the unit axiom for $N$ in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the last is naturality of $\lambda$. Cancel $\mathbf1\otimes\pi$ by step 2 to get $\gamma_Q(\eta\otimes Q)=\lambda_Q$.

For associativity put $\alpha_X=\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,X}$ and use $a$ from step 2. Bifunctoriality, step 3 and naturality give
$$\gamma_Q(\mu\otimes Q)a=\gamma_Q T\pi(\mu\otimes N)=\pi\gamma_N(\mu\otimes N),$$
whereas
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma_Q T\gamma_Q\alpha_Q a
&=\gamma_Q T\gamma_Q T^2\pi\alpha_N
=\gamma_Q T(\gamma_Q T\pi)\alpha_N\\
&=\gamma_Q T(\pi\gamma_N)\alpha_N
=\pi\gamma_N T\gamma_N\alpha_N
=\pi\gamma_N(\mu\otimes N).
\end{aligned}$$
The final equality is the associativity axiom for $N$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Cancel $a$ to obtain $\gamma_Q(\mu\otimes Q)=\gamma_Q T\gamma_Q\alpha_Q$. Together with step 4 this makes $(Q,\gamma_Q)$ a module object.

source.place: second paragraph, associativity axiom with both sides expanded

proof.text: The equation $\gamma_Q T\pi=\pi\gamma_N$ from step 3 is exactly the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] for $\pi:N\to(Q,\gamma_Q)$. Zero underlying maps are module morphisms, since $0\gamma_M=0=\gamma_N T(0)$, so $\pi f=0$ is also the zero equation in the module category. For any module object $L$ and module morphism $g:N\to L$ satisfying $gf=0$, the given underlying cokernel supplies a unique map $h:Q\to L$ in $\mathcal C$ satisfying $h\pi=g$.

source.place: third paragraph, cocone and underlying factorization

proof.text:
Using the module-morphism equation for $g$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and step 3, compute
$$h\gamma_Q T\pi=h\pi\gamma_N=g\gamma_N=\gamma_L Tg=\gamma_L Th\,T\pi.$$
Cancel $T\pi$ using step 2: $h\gamma_Q=\gamma_L Th$, so $h$ is a module morphism. If another module morphism $k$ satisfies $k\pi=g$, cancellation of $\pi$ gives $k=h$ on underlying maps; module morphisms are precisely the underlying maps satisfying the equation in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], so they are equal as module morphisms. This is the cokernel universal property in $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: third paragraph, linearity and uniqueness of the factorization

proof_origin.place: all three paragraphs; expanded universal-property arguments and corrected the epimorphism-preservation inference
